# API Requirements Quality Checklist: Create AWS Account and Track Progress

**Purpose**: Review the feature specification for complete, clear, consistent, and measurable API requirements.
**Created**: 2026-10-08
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are requirements for both submitting account-creation requests and retrieving transaction progress complete, including their distinct permissions and consumer-facing outcomes? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001–FR-003, §FR-006, §FR-012]
- [ ] CHK002 Are request-identity scope, same-request replay, changed-details conflicts, concurrent requests, and duplicate-account prevention all addressed? [Completeness, Spec §FR-004–FR-005]
- [ ] CHK003 Does the specification define a complete ordered step set, stable identifiers, consumer-understandable names, every step state, and the required transaction timestamps? [Completeness, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK004 Are success, recoverable in-progress work, terminal failure, and partial account creation all covered with their required transaction, step, and account details? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008–FR-011]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK005 Are required account fields, environment-dependent fields, configured defaults, and disallowed destinations identified clearly enough for consumers to prepare valid requests? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002, Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK006 Are “in progress,” “succeeded,” “failed,” and each step state defined so consumers can distinguish active recovery from terminal failure? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006–FR-010, User Story 2]
- [ ] CHK007 Are safe consumer-facing errors clearly distinguished for invalid input, authorization denial, unknown or expired references, and temporary progress-retrieval failure? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002, §FR-012–FR-013]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK008 Are authorization requirements consistent between creation, progress lookup, request-identity scoping, and the rule against disclosing inaccessible transactions? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004, §FR-012]
- [ ] CHK009 Are idempotency and duplicate-prevention requirements consistent across repeated requests, concurrent requests for an email, retries, and recovery? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004–FR-005, §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK010 Do overall transaction outcomes remain consistent with step states for recovery, terminal failure, timeouts, stopped work, and confirmed success? [Consistency, Spec §FR-008–FR-011]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK011 Can each success criterion be objectively assessed against a defined population or scenario, especially the 95% latency and visibility targets? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001, §SC-003]
- [ ] CHK012 Are the acceptance-time limit, progress-visibility limit, and post-termination retention period stated consistently as measurable targets and proposed defaults? [Consistency, Measurability, Spec §SC-001, §SC-003, §SC-007, Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK013 Do the success criteria provide measurable evidence for account uniqueness, correct destination, complete required steps, authorization, and stable terminal outcomes? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-004–SC-007]

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK014 Are primary, alternate, exception, and recovery requirements complete for request acceptance, progress inspection, and final outcome retrieval? [Coverage, Spec §User Stories 1–3, §FR-001–FR-015]
- [ ] CHK015 Are requirements for a newly accepted transaction and a progress snapshot during a step transition sufficient to define a coherent view of all planned work? [Coverage, Edge Case, Spec §FR-007–FR-008, Edge Cases]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK016 Are conflicting account emails, lost acceptance responses, uncertain dependency outcomes, and recovery exhaustion addressed without ambiguous duplicate-creation outcomes? [Coverage, Edge Case, Spec §FR-005, §FR-008, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK017 Are malformed or expired references, temporary lookup failures, and requests that cannot be accepted distinguished without exposing internal details or misrepresenting transaction failure? [Coverage, Clarity, Spec §FR-013, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK018 Are requirements clear for a failure after account creation, including preserving the known account identifier and defining the boundary around automatic deletion? [Coverage, Spec §FR-011, Edge Cases, Assumptions]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK019 Are confidentiality requirements explicit for both consumer-visible responses and operator diagnostics, including credentials and sensitive provisioning payloads? [Completeness, Security, Spec §FR-015]
- [ ] CHK020 Are the asynchronous acceptance, progress-visibility, and retention expectations measurable and bounded without implying a guaranteed total provisioning duration? [Clarity, Measurability, Spec §SC-001, §SC-003, §SC-007, Assumptions]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK021 Are the existing provisioning product’s required fields, mandatory steps, destinations, defaults, access, and quota dependencies documented with clear ownership and consumer-facing availability? [Dependency, Assumption, Spec §FR-002, Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK022 Are polling and the exclusions for notifications, cancellation, manual resume, deletion, and account updates explicit enough to bound the feature’s scope? [Scope, Spec §Assumptions]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [ ] CHK023 Are “safe reason,” “confirmed to exist,” and “intended ServerlessOps destination” defined with enough precision to support consistent consumer outcomes? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-009–FR-010]
- [ ] CHK024 Are the meanings of “at least 30 days,” terminal-state stability, and retention-period request-identity reuse unambiguous at the period boundary? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-004, §FR-014, §SC-007]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`.
- Add comments or findings inline and link relevant resources where useful.
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference.
